Funded by DOE’s CMEI, recent updates ensure users have the most up-to-date irradiance and meteorological information for accurate resource assessment. Researchers expanded the long-term U.S. dataset through 2024 and added coverage for polar regions, including Alaska, using polar-orbiting satellite inputs. These enhancements help energy developers, system planners, and grid operators better understand atmospheric conditions and their variability, strengthening forecasting, operations, and long-term system planning. To manage the immense data volume (roughly nine million pixels every five minutes), researchers used HPC to efficiently process, validate, and publish updated irradiance estimates. These data feed into modeling tools such as NLR’s PVWatts® and System Advisor Model™, improving their accuracy. Research published in Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews22 FORECASTING evaluated how cloud conditions influence satellite-derived resource estimates, advancing methods that improve NSRDB reliability and reduce uncertainty.
